problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Mixed-integer linear optimization: minimize c·z+d·y subject to Az+Gy≤b, with z∈ℤ^p, lo≤z≤hi, and y∈ℝ^q. The objective is linear; integrality can make the feasible set nonconvex.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Exact LP relaxation optimization oracle. A query supplies integer box endpoints; the oracle returns an exact minimizer over the original linear constraints intersected with both the original and queried boxes, or none precisely when that relaxation is infeasible. Correctness holds for every history and seed; minimizer selection may vary.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Finite dimensions p,q,m∈ℕ, with arbitrary real matrix and objective coefficients.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: All coefficients, dimensions, and integer bounds are public; there is no hidden instance. Integer variables have finite bounds, potentially inconsistent. Continuous variables need not be bounded. Validity requires only a finite lower bound on the objective over the initial LP relaxation; infeasibility is permitted.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: Exact global optimality, equivalently zero objective gap when feasible: output some feasible mixed-integer solution whose objective is no larger than that of every feasible solution. No epsilon parameter.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: Return none exactly for an infeasible mixed-integer problem; otherwise return a feasible optimal solution.

accuracy.label: deterministic
accuracy.details: Success is required for every combined algorithm and oracle seed, not merely almost surely or in expectation.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Bounded mixed-integer linear programming with exact LP relaxation solves and an exact optimum-or-infeasibility output is a standard optimization formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Bounded Mixed-Integer Linear Optimization

We consider minimizing a linear objective f:Rp×Rq→R over integer variables in Zp and continuous variables in Rq, where p,q≥0 are integers. Feasibility is specified by finitely many linear inequalities and finite integer bounds on the integer variables. The continuous relaxation has an objective bounded below on its feasible set. For any queried integer box, the oracle returns an exact optimizer of the corresponding continuous relaxation or reports infeasibility. The goal is an exact mixed-integer optimizer, or a correct infeasibility report, for every realization of any randomness.

Write the objective and feasible set as f(z,y)=c⊤z+d⊤y,F={(z,y)∈Zp×Rq:Az+Gy≤b, ℓ≤z≤u}. The optimization problem is min(z,y)∈Ff(z,y). Here m≥0 is an integer, A∈Rm×p, G∈Rm×q, b∈Rm, c∈Rp, d∈Rq, and ℓ,u∈Zp. All vector inequalities are componentwise. The algorithm receives all of these dimensions, coefficients, and bounds.

For a queried box β=(a,h)∈Zp×Zp, define its relaxation feasible set by Rβ={(z,y)∈Rp×Rq:Az+Gy≤b, ℓ≤z≤u, a≤z≤h}. Thus each query imposes its bounds in addition to the original bounds.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Lower bounded relaxation). There exists L∈R such that f(z,y)≥Lfor every (z,y)∈R(ℓ,u).

Assumption 2 (Exact relaxation oracle). Queries may be any pair β∈Zp×Zp. The oracle reports infeasibility exactly when Rβ is empty. Otherwise it returns a point (zβ,yβ) satisfying (zβ,yβ)∈Rβ,f(zβ,yβ)≤f(z,y)for every (z,y)∈Rβ. These requirements hold for every reply, including every choice among multiple optimizers.

After the allotted oracle calls, the output is either an infeasibility report or a pair (z¯,y¯)∈Zp×Rq. An infeasibility report must certify F=∅; a returned pair must satisfy (z¯,y¯)∈F,f(z¯,y¯)≤f(z,y)for every (z,y)∈F. This exact success requirement holds for every realization of the algorithm’s and oracle’s randomness.

comparisonHtml:
Minimize c⊤z+d⊤y subject to Az+Gy≤b, z∈Zp, y∈Rq, and ℓ≤z≤u, with real data and integer bounds. The root LP relaxation has objective bounded below. Each exact oracle call solves the relaxation with an additional integer box, returning any optimum or reporting infeasibility. The target is an exact global optimum or a correct infeasibility report for every seed and admissible oracle.

Exact bounded mixed-integer linear optimization: BoundedMixedIntegerLinear.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) LpBranchAndBoundMilp (Ours) (review) O(N) exact LP calls
(2) Branch-and-bound (Conforti et al. 2014) Exact node-LP oracle (1): Formalizes the classical finite-termination guarantee; no established complexity, scope, or output improvement.
(3) Exhaustive enumeration (derived bound) (Conforti et al. 2014) O(N) exact LP calls; one fixed-integer LP per box point (1): Matches known rate on the same setup and oracle. (1): Worst-case budget approaches twice the enumeration cost as N→∞; no quantified pruning gain.

Abbr: N=∏j=1p(uj−ℓj+1)+ is the number of integer box points; (t)+=max{t,0}. LP: linear program. Costs count complete exact LP solves, not arithmetic or bit operations.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Mul

namespace LongTails.Setups.BoundedMixedIntegerLinear

open OracleTemplate Matrix

structure Params where
  p : ℕ
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin p) ℝ
  G : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin q) ℝ
  b : Fin m → ℝ
  c : Fin p → ℝ
  d : Fin q → ℝ
  lo : Fin p → ℤ
  hi : Fin p → ℤ

abbrev Box (P : Params) := (Fin P.p → ℤ) × (Fin P.p → ℤ)

abbrev Point (P : Params) := (Fin P.p → ℝ) × (Fin P.q → ℝ)

abbrev Solution (P : Params) := (Fin P.p → ℤ) × (Fin P.q → ℝ)

def objective (P : Params) (x : Point P) : ℝ := P.c ⬝ᵥ x.1 + P.d ⬝ᵥ x.2

def RowFeasible (P : Params) (x : Point P) : Prop := ∀ i, (P.A *ᵥ x.1 + P.G *ᵥ x.2) i ≤ P.b i

def InBox (P : Params) (β : Box P) (z : Fin P.p → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, (β.1 j : ℝ) ≤ z j ∧ z j ≤ β.2 j

def RelaxationFeasible (P : Params) (β : Box P) (x : Point P) : Prop :=
  RowFeasible P x ∧ InBox P (P.lo, P.hi) x.1 ∧ InBox P β x.1

def toPoint (P : Params) (x : Solution P) : Point P := (fun j => (x.1 j : ℝ), x.2)

def MixedFeasible (P : Params) (x : Solution P) : Prop :=
  RowFeasible P (toPoint P x) ∧ ∀ j, P.lo j ≤ x.1 j ∧ x.1 j ≤ P.hi j

def SolvesRelaxation (P : Params) (β : Box P) : Option (Point P) → Prop
  | none => ∀ x, ¬ RelaxationFeasible P β x
  | some x => RelaxationFeasible P β x ∧
      ∀ x', RelaxationFeasible P β x' → objective P x ≤ objective P x'

def IsRelaxationOracle (P : Params) (O : Oracle (Box P) (Option (Point P))) : Prop :=
  ∀ history (query : Fin 1 × Box P) seed, SolvesRelaxation P query.2 (O.answer history query seed)

def SolvesMixed (P : Params) : Option (Solution P) → Prop
  | none => ∀ x, ¬ MixedFeasible P x
  | some x => MixedFeasible P x ∧
      ∀ x', MixedFeasible P x' → objective P (toPoint P x) ≤ objective P (toPoint P x')

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance _ := Unit
  Query P := Box P
  Reply P := Option (Point P)
  Output P := Option (Solution P)
  publicInput P := P
  valid P := ∃ L, ∀ x, RelaxationFeasible P (P.lo, P.hi) x → L ≤ objective P x
  admissible P _ O := IsRelaxationOracle P O
  successful P _ output _ := ∀ ω, SolvesMixed P (output ω)

end LongTails.Setups.BoundedMixedIntegerLinear
